ingredients.intro: One botanical, named in Latin on the listing, and a label that stops there. Here is the tree, the question of which part of it is in the capsule, and the figures that are missing.

cards.alt: The trunk of a Bursera simaruba, coppery bark peeling away in thin papery sheets
cards.p: A fast growing tree of the Caribbean, southern Florida, Mexico and Central America, at home on limestone and along the edges of dry forest. The bark is smooth and coppery and lifts away in thin papery sheets, which is how you place it at a distance and where its nicknames come from. It is often used as a living fence post, because a cut branch pushed into the ground will take root and grow.

cards.alt: Loose capsules and a wooden scoop on dark slate
cards.p: Bark and leaf are the two parts this tree is traded for, and they are not the same material. Our listing names the species, calls the contents 100 per cent pure, and never says pure what. So this page does not say either. The capsules in the picture are a generated scene rather than a photograph of ours.

cards.alt: Clove buds, black peppercorns and a pale flecked powder in three small bowls on a wooden sill, a generated scene
cards.p: There are no milligrams a capsule on this listing and no capsule count either, which between them make a serving weight and a cost a day impossible to work out. The bowls in the picture are a generated scene and none of the powder in them is ours.

cards.alt: Two plain capsules on a saucer beside a glass of water, a generated scene
cards.p: The listing prints no fillers and no additives, and it does not say what the shell is made from or whether it is vegan. Several of our other jars print that mark. This one does not, so it is not on the sheet below.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: The species is named in Latin and both schedules are printed exactly as the listing prints them. The count, the milligrams and the part of the tree are named as missing rather than estimated, and the arithmetic that would guess the count is shown once and then kept off the sheet. What gumbo limbo does in a person is not something we are permitted to say. The live listing says a great deal about it, and none of that has been carried over here.

reiss.label: Reiss's turn
paras: Both schedules on this listing come to forty capsules. Two in the morning and two at night for ten days is forty. Two a day for twenty days is forty. That is not a coincidence and anybody who has ever filled a jar can see what it means. It still does not go on the sheet, because a number I worked out on the back of an envelope is not a number you can hold the jar against.

The rest of what is missing is more ordinary and more irritating. No milligrams. No part of the tree, which matters here more than it does on most labels, because gumbo limbo is traded as bark and as leaf and the two are different material at different prices. At £29.99 this is the top of our single botanical range and it carries one of the thinnest labels on the shelf, which is the wrong way round and is on my list.

The tree itself I will happily talk about all afternoon. You see them across the Caribbean, coppery and peeling, and people push cut branches into the ground as fence posts because the branches root and turn into trees. What the capsules do once you have swallowed them is not mine to tell you, and I will not guess at it the way I will not guess at the count.
reiss.pull: A number worked out on the back of an envelope is not a specification.
